```{r setup, include=FALSE}
extra_lib <- Sys.getenv("CELLADMIX_R_LIB", "")
if (nzchar(extra_lib)) {
  .libPaths(c(extra_lib, .libPaths()))
}

library(cellAdmixCore)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center", dpi = 96, fig.retina = 2)
options(width = 110, scipen = 999)
tile_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

This page draws the diagnostic panels of the multi-sample workflow for
the two Xenium breast replicates: for every stage, each sample's own
result against the consensus. It is the companion of the
[worked example](breast_replicates_multisample.md), which explains the
workflow and the tables the panels are built from; the panels here are
the views that separate the ways a shared treatment can fail. Every
panel puts the samples on one axis, so the figures read the same with
two sections or twenty.

The objects are rebuilt from the caches the worked example left in the
samples' output directories.

```{r objects, results="hide"}
read_labels <- function(path) {
  labels <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  labels <- labels[labels$cell_type != "Unlabeled", ]
  setNames(labels$cell_type, labels$cell_id)
}
labels <- list(
  rep1 = read_labels(file.path("annotations", "rep1_annotation.csv.gz")),
  rep2 = read_labels(file.path("annotations", "rep2_annotation.csv.gz")))
datasets <- list(
  rep1 = cellAdmix("data/rep1", output_dir = "out/rep1", annotation = labels$rep1, num_threads = 8),
  rep2 = cellAdmix("data/rep2", output_dir = "out/rep2", annotation = labels$rep2, num_threads = 8))
collection <- cellAdmixCollection(datasets)
collection$fit(nmf_variant = "ls_nmf")
consensus <- collection$fit_consensus()
score <- consensus$score_bridge()
rules <- score$rules()
correction <- score$correct(rules = rules, num_threads = 32)
audit <- consensus$audit_admixture()
report <- audit$evaluate(correction)
samples <- consensus$samples()
```

## Factor space

```{r factor-space, fig.width=13, fig.height=10}
# (a) each sample's restarts and primary factor against every shared factor
recurrence <- consensus$recurrence()
matching <- consensus$matching
key <- function(df) paste(df$sample, df$consensus_factor)
recurrence$correlation <- matching$correlation[match(key(recurrence), key(matching))]
recurrence$label <- ifelse(is.na(recurrence$correlation), "", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", recurrence$correlation)))
p_map <- ggplot(recurrence, aes(x = factor(consensus_factor), y = sample, fill = recurrence)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey97", high = "steelblue4", limits = c(0, 1), name = "share of\nrestarts") +
  labs(x = "shared factor", y = NULL, title = "Shared factors in each sample",
    subtitle = "fill: share of the sample's restarts carrying the program;\ntext: ownership correlation of the sample's primary factor with the shared profile") +
  tile_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

# (b) every primary factor: its molecule share against its own stability
importance <- function(fit) {
  cells <- fit$cell_factors()
  cols <- grep("^factor_[0-9]+_fraction$", names(cells), value = TRUE)
  weights <- cells$transcript_count
  data.frame(sample_factor = as.integer(sub("^factor_([0-9]+)_fraction$", "\\1", cols)),
    importance = vapply(cols, function(col) sum(cells[[col]] * weights) / sum(weights), numeric(1)))
}
primaries <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(s) {
  imp <- importance(consensus$own_fits[[s]])
  m <- matching[matching$sample == s, ]
  m$importance <- imp$importance[match(m$sample_factor, imp$sample_factor)]
  m
}))
primaries$status <- ifelse(primaries$matched, "in the shared space", "not reproduced")
p_lost <- ggplot(primaries, aes(x = 100 * importance, y = own_stability, color = status, shape = sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = primaries[!primaries$matched, ],
    aes(label = paste0(sample, " f", sample_factor)), size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("in the shared space" = "steelblue4", "not reproduced" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "share of the sample's molecules (%)", y = "stability within the sample's restarts",
    color = NULL, shape = NULL, title = "Each sample's primary factors",
    subtitle = "a program the consensus dropped is harmless when small and unstable") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")

# (c) representation cost and shared fraction per sample
diagnostics <- consensus$diagnostics()
p_cost <- ggplot(diagnostics, aes(x = sample)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = -100 * restart_spread, ymax = 100 * restart_spread), color = "grey55", linewidth = 2.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = 100 * loss_gap, color = representation_flag), size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 100 * restart_spread, label = sprintf("%d of %d primaries shared", primary_factors_shared, primary_factors)),
    vjust = -0.8, size = 2.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "steelblue4", "TRUE" = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.5))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "loss gap (%)", title = "Representation cost per sample",
    subtitle = "point: loss under the shared profiles relative to the sample's own;\nbar: the spread of the sample's own restarts") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10)

# (d) factor usage divergence per cell type and sample
divergence <- consensus$usage_divergence(by_sample = TRUE)
p_usage <- ggplot(divergence, aes(x = sample, y = reorder(cell_type, divergence), fill = divergence)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", divergence)), size = 2.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey97", high = "darkorange3", name = "usage\ndivergence") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Factor usage against the pool",
    subtitle = "half the L1 distance between the sample's and the pooled usage") +
  tile_theme

plot_grid(p_map, p_lost, p_cost, p_usage, ncol = 2, labels = "auto", rel_heights = c(1, 1.15))
```

**Figure 1. Each sample's factorization against the consensus.** (a) For
every shared factor, the share of each sample's restarts that found the
program and, written in the tile, how closely the sample's own primary
factor matches the shared profile. A dark tile with a high number is a
program every sample finds in the same form; a dark tile with a low
number is a program the sample finds but in a different form (a split or
a chimera in one of the fits); a pale tile is a program the sample
rarely or never finds on its own. (b) Every primary factor of every
sample by its share of the sample's molecules and its stability across
the sample's own restarts; the factors the consensus did not keep are
named. A dropped program that is small and unstable costs nothing; a
dropped program that is large or stable is a sample-specific program
that will not be cleaned. (c) The loss gap of each sample under the
shared profiles against the spread of its own restarts; a point inside
or below the bar means the consensus describes the sample as well as one
of its own restarts would. (d) For every cell type and sample, how far the
sample's use of the shared factors for that type departs from the pooled
use; a column that stands out marks a sample in which a type is labeled
differently, a sample effect in the labeling.

## Shared profiles that fit least well

```{r profiles, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.6}
genes <- colnames(consensus$profiles)
own_loading <- function(s, shared_factor) {
  m <- matching[which(matching$sample == s & matching$consensus_factor == shared_factor), ]
  if (!nrow(m)) return(NULL)
  h <- consensus$own_fits[[s]]$loadings()
  colnames(h) <- consensus$own_fits[[s]]$run$genes
  h[m$sample_factor[[1]], genes]
}
shared <- consensus$factors
joined_by_all <- as.integer(names(which(table(matching$consensus_factor[matching$matched]) == length(samples))))
shared <- shared[shared$consensus_factor %in% joined_by_all, ]
worst <- head(shared$consensus_factor[order(shared$agreement)], 3)
profile_panels <- lapply(worst, function(k) {
  df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(s) {
    own <- own_loading(s, k)
    if (is.null(own)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(sample = s, gene = genes, consensus = consensus$profiles[k, ], own = own)
  }))
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  df$difference <- abs(df$own - df$consensus)
  marked <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(df, df$sample), function(d) head(d[order(-d$difference), ], 5)))
  ggplot(df, aes(x = consensus, y = own, color = sample)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
    geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = marked, aes(label = gene), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "shared profile loading", y = "sample's own primary loading", color = NULL,
      title = sprintf("shared factor %d (agreement %.2f)", k,
        shared$agreement[shared$consensus_factor == k])) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
})
plot_grid(plotlist = Filter(Negate(is.null), profile_panels), ncol = 3)
```

**Figure 2. The shared profiles with the lowest within-cluster
agreement among those every sample's primary factor joined**, each as
the gene loadings of every sample's own primary factor against the
shared profile, with the five genes each sample disagrees on most named. Genes off the diagonal in one sample only are
what that sample's version of the program carries that the consensus
does not, or the reverse; they say whether the disagreement is a
biological difference between the sections or a factorization artifact
such as a split program.

## Scoring: per-sample evidence against the pooled call

```{r scoring, fig.width=14, fig.height=9}
p_thresh <- 0.1
pooled <- score$summary()
per_sample <- score$sample_summaries()
n_samples <- length(samples)

# (a) pooled significance per cell type and factor, with the number of
# samples whose own evidence passes the threshold written in each call
cell_pooled <- aggregate(neg_log10_p ~ target_cell_type + factor, pooled, max)
cell_sample <- aggregate(p_value ~ sample + target_cell_type + factor, per_sample, min)
cell_sample$passes <- cell_sample$p_value < p_thresh
support <- aggregate(passes ~ target_cell_type + factor, cell_sample, sum)
cell_pooled$passing <- support$passes[match(paste(cell_pooled$target_cell_type, cell_pooled$factor),
  paste(support$target_cell_type, support$factor))]
kept_calls <- unique(paste(rules$factor[rules$keep], rules$target_cell_type[rules$keep]))
candidate_calls <- unique(paste(rules$factor, rules$target_cell_type))
cell_key <- paste(cell_pooled$factor, cell_pooled$target_cell_type)
cell_pooled$label <- ifelse(cell_key %in% kept_calls, sprintf("%d/%d", cell_pooled$passing, n_samples),
  ifelse(cell_key %in% candidate_calls, sprintf("(%d/%d)", cell_pooled$passing, n_samples), ""))
cell_pooled$fill <- pmin(cell_pooled$neg_log10_p, 6)
p_calls <- ggplot(cell_pooled, aes(x = factor(factor), y = target_cell_type, fill = fill)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick", limits = c(0, 6), name = "pooled\n-log10 p") +
  labs(x = "shared factor", y = NULL, title = "Removal calls and their support",
    subtitle = sprintf("text: samples passing p < %g, of %d; in parentheses: vetoed by the native-factor check", p_thresh, n_samples)) +
  tile_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

# (b) the kept rules that lack local evidence in at least one sample
partial <- rules[rules$keep & rules$sample_support < 1, ]
partial$rule <- sprintf("f%d %s → %s", partial$factor, partial$source_cell_type, partial$target_cell_type)
rule_key <- function(df) paste(df$factor, df$source_cell_type, df$target_cell_type)
local <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(s) {
  ps <- per_sample[per_sample$sample == s, ]
  data.frame(sample = s, rule = partial$rule, pooled = partial$neg_log10_p,
    local = ps$neg_log10_p[match(rule_key(partial), rule_key(ps))])
}))
local$local[is.na(local$local)] <- 0
local$rule <- factor(local$rule, levels = partial$rule[order(partial$neg_log10_p)])
p_partial <- ggplot(local, aes(x = sample, y = rule, fill = pmin(local, 6))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", local)), size = 2.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq_len(n_samples) + 0.5, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick", limits = c(0, 6), name = "sample\n-log10 p") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Kept rules without local evidence in some sample",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d kept rules; rows ordered by pooled significance", nrow(partial), sum(rules$keep))) +
  tile_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

plot_grid(p_calls, p_partial, ncol = 2, labels = "auto", rel_widths = c(1.35, 1))
```

**Figure 3. Pooled calls against each sample's own evidence.** (a) The
pooled scoring matrix with each removal call annotated by the number of
samples whose own scoring passes the threshold for that cell type and
factor; a call carried by few samples rests on the pool, which is the
intended uniform treatment of replicates but a point to examine in a
cohort. Calls in parentheses were proposed by the scores and vetoed by
the native-factor check. (b) The kept rules that at least one sample's
own scoring does not support, with each sample's significance; a sample
whose column is pale throughout is the one whose cleanup rests most on
the other samples' evidence.

## Correction and verification per sample

```{r cleanup, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# (a) share of each sample's removal attributed to each shared factor
removal_by_factor <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(s) {
  removed <- cellAdmixCore:::.celladmix_removed_by_type_factor(consensus$fits[[s]], correction$corrections[[s]])
  by_factor <- aggregate(removed ~ factor, removed, sum)
  data.frame(sample = s, factor = by_factor$factor, share = by_factor$removed / sum(by_factor$removed))
}))
p_factor <- ggplot(removal_by_factor, aes(x = factor(factor), y = sample, fill = 100 * share)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * share)), size = 2.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey97", high = "darkorange3", name = "% of the\nsample's\nremoval") +
  labs(x = "shared factor", y = NULL, title = "Removal attributed to each shared factor",
    subtitle = "a factor dark in one sample only removes a program that sample's restarts may not carry") +
  tile_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

# (b) cleanup sensitivity of the largest pairs in every sample
pairs <- report$pairs()
pair_size <- aggregate(admixed_molecules ~ source + target, pairs, sum)
top <- head(pair_size[order(-pair_size$admixed_molecules), ], 30)
pairs$pair <- paste(pairs$source, "→", pairs$target)
top_pairs <- pairs[paste(pairs$source, pairs$target) %in% paste(top$source, top$target), ]
top_pairs$pair <- factor(top_pairs$pair, levels = rev(paste(top$source, "→", top$target)))
p_sens <- ggplot(top_pairs, aes(x = sample, y = pair, fill = pmax(pmin(sensitivity, 1), 0))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", sensitivity)), size = 2.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "seagreen4", limits = c(0, 1), name = "sensitivity") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Cleanup sensitivity of the 30 largest pairs",
    subtitle = "pale in every sample: a pair the rules do not cover; pale in one: that sample's problem") +
  tile_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

# (c) own-marker false removal per cell type and sample
false_removal <- do.call(rbind, lapply(samples, function(s) {
  fr <- report$reports[[s]]$false_removal()
  fr$sample <- s
  fr
}))
p_false <- ggplot(false_removal, aes(x = 100 * false_removal, y = reorder(cell_type, false_removal), color = sample)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  labs(x = "own-marker false removal (%)", y = NULL, color = NULL,
    title = "Own-marker false removal per cell type",
    subtitle = "molecules of a type's own markers removed from its cells far from any source") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# (d) the headline verification numbers per sample
headline <- report$summary()
headline <- rbind(
  data.frame(sample = headline$sample, measure = "leakage removed", value = headline$leakage_removed_overall),
  data.frame(sample = headline$sample, measure = "median pair sensitivity", value = headline$median_pair_sensitivity),
  data.frame(sample = headline$sample, measure = "own-marker false removal", value = headline$own_marker_false_removal))
headline$measure <- factor(headline$measure, levels = c("leakage removed", "median pair sensitivity", "own-marker false removal"))
limits <- data.frame(measure = rep(levels(headline$measure), each = 2),
  value = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, max(0.05, max(headline$value[headline$measure == "own-marker false removal"]))))
limits$measure <- factor(limits$measure, levels = levels(headline$measure))
p_headline <- ggplot(headline, aes(x = sample, y = value)) +
  geom_blank(data = limits, aes(y = value), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Verification summary per sample") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10)

plot_grid(p_factor, p_sens, p_false, p_headline, ncol = 2, labels = "auto", rel_heights = c(1, 1.2))
```

**Figure 4. The correction and its verification in each sample.** (a)
How each sample's removal distributes over the shared factors; a factor
that takes a large share in one sample only is removing a program that
sample's own restarts may not carry, the quantity the correction
diagnostics report as removal via absent programs. (b) The cleanup
sensitivity of the largest cell-type pairs in every sample: a row that is
pale in all samples is a pair the rules do not cover, a method
limitation; a cell that is pale in one sample is that sample's problem.
(c) The own-marker false removal of every cell type in every sample, one
point per sample. The two hybrid types of this annotation lose most of
their own markers: their markers are those of the two types each
combines, which the correction treats as admixture in them. (d) The three headline numbers of the verification per
sample.
